candidate.answerReason: The centers form an equilateral triangle of side 4 and area \(4\sqrt3\). Subtracting its three 60° sectors leaves a gap of area \(4\sqrt3-2\pi\). Adding the three disks gives \(10\pi+4\sqrt3\).

methods.label: Find the central gap
methods.explanation:
Join the three circle centers to make a triangle. External tangency makes each center distance \(2+2=4\), so this triangle is equilateral and has three \(60^\circ\) angles.

[Figure 1](figures/2012_AMC_10B_Q16_question_fig1.svg)

An altitude divides the triangle into two right triangles with hypotenuse \(4\) and one leg \(2\). Its height is therefore
\[
\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt3,
\]
and its area is \(\frac12\cdot4\cdot2\sqrt3=4\sqrt3\).

Inside the center triangle, each circle occupies a \(60^\circ\) sector. The three sectors have total area
\[
3\left(\frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ}\pi\cdot2^2\right)=2\pi.
\]
The remaining part of the triangle is exactly the central curved gap, so its area is \(4\sqrt3-2\pi\).

The three disks have disjoint interiors and total area \(3\pi\cdot2^2=12\pi\). The gap lies outside all three disks, so adding it counts every part of the shaded region once:
\[
12\pi+(4\sqrt3-2\pi)
=\boxed{10\pi+4\sqrt3}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
